laws.rule: From 1 April 2026, top-tier parks (including Etosha, Namib-Naukluft, Dorob, Skeleton Coast, Waterberg, Cape Cross): nationals of non-SADC foreign countries aged 16 and over pay N$280 a day (N$140 park entrance plus N$140 conservation fee); ages 9 to 15 N$180; 8 and under free. Vehicles with 10 seats or less N$60. (No RBA rate for NAD; at the Bank of Namibia rate of 30 October 2026 (at par with ZAR), crossed via the South African Reserve Bank ZAR rate and the RBA USD rate of 30 October 2026, A$1 = about 11.7177 NAD: N$280 ≈ A$23.90; N$140 ≈ A$11.95; N$180 ≈ A$15.36; N$60 ≈ A$5.12)
laws.heading: Government Notice 115 of 2026

laws.rule: For Welwitschia Drive and Sandwich Harbour, MEFT's park-permit FAQ says permits must be obtained beforehand. It separately says through-travel on the main road through Namib-Naukluft does not require a park permit. The ministry lists its offices and says Namibia Wildlife Resorts does not issue permits. Check the current issuing office and route: ordinary through-road travel is not permission to leave that route.
